subject: Availability guardrail amendment request + order form ops playbook
messages:
From: Sanjay Agarwal <sanjay.agarwal@medicor-labs.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@medicor-labs.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: availability guardrail language + operational playbook

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week — we liked Redwood's latency profile and the quantization options. Before we can move to signature, our procurement and SRE teams asked for a small rider to the MSA that clarifies availability guardrails and a handoff-runbook for degraded-mode operations. Specifically they want: 

- A short exhibit that documents acceptable degraded-mode behavior (e.g., 2-tier fallback to a smaller instance class, maximum burst queueing latency before a credit is applied).
- A concise ops playbook (1–2 pages) that our SREs can follow during an outage — notification flow, failover checklist, and the contact escalation path.
- Evidence we meet the regional availability targets for US-east over the last 90 days (SLA telemetry summary).

Can your team provide proposed exhibit language and an ops-runbook template we can hand to our SREs? Also let me know whether this requires an order-form amendment or a separate rider to the SOW. We are on a tight procurement cycle and would like to close by Aug 10th.

Appreciate it —
Sanjay
Procurement / Medicor Labs

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Agarwal <sanjay.agarwal@medicor-labs.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability guardrail language + operational playbook

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear checklist. We can absolutely provide a short exhibit and an ops-runbook draft. Quick notes on the asks:

- Exhibit vs order form: for the guardrail language we typically attach an "Availability Exhibit" as an Order Form annex (simpler for billing/credits). If Medicor prefers a rider to the MSA we can do that, but it usually slows procurement by a week.
- Ops playbook: we have a 2-page template (attached) that covers notification windows, who owns failover steps, and how traffic is routed to fallback model variants. We'll tailor it to your instance topology.
- Evidence: we can provide a 90-day availability snapshot for the us-east region and a short note on our regional fallback policy.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send a draft Availability Exhibit (order-form annex) + ops-runbook template by EOD today.
2) Monica will follow up with a redline-friendly Word version of the exhibit for your legal/procurement.
3) If you need it as an MSA rider instead, flag that and we’ll loop legal.

We aim to have a DocuSign-ready package if all looks good.

Best,
David Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Agarwal <sanjay.agarwal@medicor-labs.com>, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jul 2028 13:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Drafts: Availability Exhibit (order-form annex) + ops-runbook template — attached

Sanjay — forwarding the drafts as promised. Attachments included: Medicor_SLA_Guardrail_Rider_v1.docx (word, redline-friendly), RI-ops-runbook-template.pdf (ops playbook), Medicor-OrderForm-Draft.xlsx (order form with exhibit references).

Key callouts in the exhibit (short summary):
- Guardrail definition: "Degraded mode" defined as sustained per-request P95 latency > 2x target for > 3 minutes across > 5% of requests over a 5‑minute window.
- Fallback behavior: automatic routing to a quantized model variant in the same region; maximum queueing time before shedding is 250ms; customer is eligible for service credit tiers starting at 2% of monthly invoice for availability below 99.5%.
- Operational handoff: we include an "Ops Escalation" table with a primary/secondary contact and a 15-minute initial response SLA for severity-1 incidents (note — response SLA is for communication, not a financial SLA).

Evidence note: we have attached a 90-day availability export for us-east (redacted) and a short write-up on fallback tests. Monica (cc) can share the telemetry slice for the time window you need.

If procurement wants the guardrail embedded in the MSA rather than the order form annex, we can prepare rider language but will need legal review (adds ~3 business days).

Monica Patel
Enterprise Contracts | Redwood Inference
Attachments: Medicor_SLA_Guardrail_Rider_v1.docx (word), RI-ops-runbook-template.pdf (pdf), Medicor-OrderForm-Draft.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Sanjay Agarwal <sanjay.agarwal@medicor-labs.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 31 Jul 2028 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Drafts: Availability Exhibit (order-form annex) + ops-runbook template — attached

Thanks Monica / David — received and reviewed quickly with our SRE lead. A few follow-ups: 

- The degraded-mode threshold looks reasonable, but our SREs asked whether the 250ms max queueing is measured at the load balancer vs at the application layer. Can you confirm the measurement point?
- Procurement prefers an order-form annex (not an MSA rider) — that matches your suggestion. Please provide the Word redline-ready doc (you mentioned it's attached).
- Can you add a short paragraph in the ops playbook that lists the monitoring alerts (metric names) our on-call will see and the recommended playbook step per alert? That will make it handoff-ready.

If we can get updated docs today, we'll route to procurement and aim to sign the order-form by Aug 9. Also please include the DocuSign link when ready.

Best,
Sanjay
Procurement / Medicor Labs
